title: Variable refresh rate (VRR) performance issue under Gnome 50 (Wayland)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.10.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 26.04 (Wayland)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Apologies in advance for the peculiar bug-report, but this truly appears to be an Electron related issue...

Setup is as follows: Laptop with an internal 2.8k-screen, variable refresh rate (VRR) enabled; an external 4k-monitor (its VRR state seems irrelevant). Both screens are in-use.

Run two Electron-based apps; one on either monitor; both of their windows maximised (not full-screen).

I would expect the (drawing) performance of both applications to be identical, and to be good/"smooth".

### Actual Behavior

It is not.

Performance of the maximised window on the laptop's screen is terrible (feels like "15 FPS"). The moment the Electron app on the other/external monitor goes from maximised the windowed, performance of the maximised window on the laptop screen returns to normal.

In other words: Performance is as expected in all situations, _except_ when two Electron-based apps run with maximised windows on the two separate monitors (where one has VRR enabled; the VRR state of the other screen seems not to matter).

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

This screen capture illustrates the problem perhaps better than the above description:
- https://drive.proton.me/urls/HTKT29NV30#2mE6vTjCMBDe – 5k h264 (Firefox doesn't seem to want to play it; Chromium has no problems)

The effect is diminished in the capture as a result of the load put on the system by capturing. The difference in v-sync performance is still pretty obvious though. The external monitor is on the top left, the laptop's screen on the bottom right.

Identical behaviour is observed with other (recent) Electron apps (Joplin, Electron 42; Slack, Electron 44). VS Code offers the easiest reproduction as one can simply run [vsynctester.com](https://www.vsynctester.com/) in its internal browser. Any combination of VS Code, Joplin, and Slack (so I would assume "any" Electron-based app) can be used to reproduce the issue.

The problem does not occur with Chromium itself (tested with ungoogled-chromium `152.0.7977.82`), nor with other applications (i.e., Firefox works fine too).

Disabling VRR on the laptop's screen resolves the issue.

The converse setup (laptop screen with VRR disabled; 4k-monitor with VRR enabled) doesn't exhibit the issue either. Perhaps a result of the difference in VRR ranges?

- Laptop screen: 30-120 Hz
- 4k-monitor: 48-120 Hz
